mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate of 0.08% is at a historically low level, and historical data shows that such low rates are associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to compressed discount rates and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% within a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger a flight to quality and positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors seek safe havens in equities during economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% within a 3-month window, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and UNRATE > 4.8%) signals a tightening monetary policy that is causing labor market stress, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as the market anticipates a potential policy pivot to ease.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and UNRATE > 4.8%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
